match.reason: The bank point teaches linking a question's idea to a technique and its effect in body paragraphs, while the new point is about how to write an introduction (naming the text and writer, giving a contention, and mapping the main points), so no bank point teaches the same idea.

draft.title: Writing an introduction
card: An introduction opens a text response. It names the text and its writer, so the reader knows what is being discussed.
It then answers the topic with a contention. A contention is the one clear argument the whole essay will defend. It should respond to the words of the topic, not just repeat them.
Next it maps the main points. This is a short preview of the ideas, in order, that the body paragraphs will cover.
An introduction is brief. It does not retell the plot or give detailed evidence, because the body paragraphs do that.
draft.remember: Name the text and writer, state a contention, then preview the main points.

a.q: What is the job of the contention in an introduction?
opts: To state the argument the essay will defend
To retell the opening of the text
To list the quotes the essay will use
To explain who the writer is
a.why: The contention is the clear answer to the topic that the essay argues. Retelling the plot is wrong because an introduction does not give detailed events, which belong to the body.
a.clue: It is the answer to the topic.

b.q: Which sentence in an introduction maps the main points?
opts: First, the writer shows guilt, and then the cost of silence
Many readers enjoy this novel and its memorable characters
The novel was published after years of careful drafting
The topic asks whether the main character is truly guilty
b.why: The first option previews the ideas the body paragraphs will cover, in order. The last option only restates the topic, so it does not preview the argument's points.
b.clue: Look for a preview of ideas in order.

a.best: To state the argument the essay will defend

b.best: First, the writer shows guilt, and then the cost of silence

problems.detail: Why (b) points to options by position ('the first option', 'the last option'), but the options are shuffled. As shown, the mapping sentence is third, and the option that restates the topic is first, not last. A student reading this why would be confused about which sentence is right.
